subject: HealthGrid DPA / transfers / KMS — clarifications and artifacts
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: legal@healthgrid.com, gdpr-ops@healthgrid.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPA and data handling — HealthGrid evaluation

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — we were impressed by the throughput numbers. Our privacy and procurement teams have started a formal evaluation and they sent over a security questionnaire (attached). Before we dive into the full SSQ, can you help with three immediate items we need to validate for our legal/compliance review: 

1) A current list of subprocessors that may have access to PII (including region and purpose).
2) A simple data flow diagram showing how customer PII flows from ingestion -> inference -> logs/export (including where KMS keys live).
3) Clarification on transfer mechanisms for EU data (do you rely on SCCs, adequacy, or customer-managed keys in EU-only regions?).

Also — do you have a short attestation or artifact showing KMS key custody and exportability controls (our security team wants to see whether keys can be exported or if they are HSM-bound)?

Can you confirm estimated turnaround? We need initial artifacts for our vendor panel by the end of next week.

Appreciate it,

Marco Ruiz
Head of Integrations, HealthGrid
marco.ruiz@healthgrid.com
[Attachment: HealthGrid_SSQ_Request_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 95 KB)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@healthgrid.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.example.com, marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and data handling — HealthGrid evaluation

Hi Marco —

Thanks for the clear list and the SSQ. I'll loop in Priyom (privacy ops) and Marcus (infrastructure) — they can produce the artifacts. High-level answers now: we publish our subprocessors inventory and provide a data flow diagram for onboarding customers; we support SCCs and also offer EU-region hosting. For KMS: by default keys are managed by Redwood with HSM protections, but Dedicated/Private customers can use customer-managed keys.

Priyom / Marcus — can you prepare: 
- the subprocessors CSV scoped to HealthGrid (region & purpose)
- a simplified dataflow diagram (png) showing KMS location(s) and where PII may persist
- a short KMS custody note / attestation stub we can share for the panel

Marco — is there a subset of questions in the SSQ you want us to prioritize (e.g., data transfers, KMS, SOC2 evidence)?

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
[Attachment: none]

From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@healthgrid.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA and data handling — HealthGrid evaluation (artifacts)

Hi all —

Attached are the initial artifacts for HealthGrid. Summary below; full answers are in the attached spreadsheet and the diagram.

Attachments: 
- redwood-dataflow-healthgrid.png (simplified PII flow diagram)
- Redwood_DPA_v1.2.pdf (current DPA draft we typically send)
- redwood-kms-attestation-stub.txt (short note on KMS custody)

Key points (TL;DR):
- PII categories: user identifiers, contact info (name/email), device identifiers, inference input (customer-provided content that may include PII). We do not persist inference outputs long-term by default unless customer opt-in for logging/retention.
- Access controls: role-based access (RBAC) with least privilege; SRE and infra admins require logged justification & short-lived elevated sessions. Audit logs retained per contract.
- Subprocessors: (we will provide a CSV in the next hour). High-level: cloud providers (compute/storage), monitoring/observability vendors, and a managed KMS partner for hosted HSMs. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) — in those cases Redwood does not have exportable access to key material.
- Transfers: For EU -> non-EU transfers we rely on SCCs. We also offer EU-only tenancy and on-prem appliance for customers requiring no cross-border transfers.

For the KMS attestation: the stub explains that hosted HSM keys are provisioned in HSM-backed KMS; private keys are non-exportable and held within an HSM boundary. We can provide a redacted attestation from our KMS vendor by EOW.

Next steps proposed: 
1) We’ll share the subprocessors CSV + updated diagram within today.
2) If HealthGrid wants, we can prepare a DPA addendum (EU-only processing clause) and a DocuSign-ready DPA within 10 business days.

Date: Sat, 13 Sep 2025 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and data handling — HealthGrid evaluation

Thanks Priyom — this is helpful. A few clarifying asks from procurement/security: 

- Can you confirm whether audit logs showing KMS key usage (key wrap/unwrap events) can be exported for a customer's audit? If not, can you provide a KMS vendor attestation we can accept?
- For subprocessors: we need to confirm whether any subprocessor could access raw inference inputs in plain text (e.g., for feature engineering, labeling, or support). Please flag any subprocessors that have potential plaintext access.
- DPA: HealthGrid’s legal team will want SCCs attached and a clause for EU-only processing (if we contract for EU tenancy). Is Redwood able to sign an addendum limiting cross-border exports to exceptional, documented cases?

I’ve attached our scoring sheet (HealthGrid_SSQ_Request_v1.xlsx) with highlighted rows for priority questions. If you can return the prioritized sections (KMS evidence, subprocessor access, and transfer clause) by next Wednesday (2025-09-17) that would keep us on the vendor panel timeline.

Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA and data handling — HealthGrid evaluation (next steps)

Hi Marco —

Thanks for the priority flags. To keep the vendor panel timeline we propose the following deliverables and dates: 

1) Today (sent): subprocessors CSV + simplified dataflow diagram + KMS attestation stub (redwood-kms-attestation-stub.txt).
2) By EOW (2025-09-19): redacted KMS vendor attestation and SOC2 cert copy for your legal team to review.
3) By 10 business days (target 2025-09-26): DocuSign-ready DPA + optional EU-only addendum (we can toggle an EU-residency clause and attach SCCs as exhibits).

On the specific asks: 
- KMS logs: we can export key usage metadata (wrap/unwrap events) at the API level for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted customers we provide vendor attestation and audit extracts on request (we'll include the redacted attestation in the EOW packet).
- Subprocessor plaintext access: we flagged all subprocessors with potential plaintext access in the CSV; monitoring vendors do not receive inference inputs in plaintext. Any support access to content is tightly controlled and logged — we marked those rows and the justified purpose.
- DPA export limitations: we can sign an EU-only processing addendum for EU tenancy; for hosted multi-region contracts we require documented exceptions for exports. We'll draft both options and let your legal pick.

If that timeline works I’ll open a DocuSign packet and include the primary signatories: Marco Ruiz (HealthGrid) and Kimberly Park (Redwood). Please let us know if HealthGrid legal wants a different signatory list.

Best regards,

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
